summaryForMax:
Headless verification is strong: AC-0/1/2/3/7 (the module move, fluvial-family wiring, byte-identical routing, relief/crater display math, and the bake-host worker protocol) all came back PASS against the real test suite, with only pre-existing/unrelated failures elsewhere (the tracked LOD-octave-ramp saturation and moon-corpus-count drift — neither touches rivers).

What's NOT yet verified is anything live in the browser. Three ACs now hinge on that:
- AC-4 (relief/crater bake actually changes pixels) and AC-5 (rivers ribbon actually shows/hides) are integration-layer ACs that require a live chrome-devtools drive — this is working-Claude's job, not yours. It needs: load a Rocky (Earthlike) body, press U (relief toggle) and J (rivers toggle), confirm the visuals change as the contract describes.
- AC-6 (the "did anything unrelated break" reconciliation) had a clean headless pass, but adversarial review flagged that its own observable text also names a live-Chrome check (route() binding a real cube set, Rivers toggle showing the ribbon) that wasn't driven — fold that into the same live pass as AC-4/AC-5 rather than treating it as a separate gap.

Once those live checks are green, AC-8 is yours alone to judge: open the live build on a procedural system, fly up to a wet solid body, and while moving press J (rivers) then U (relief) and watch whether it reads right to your eye. No agent can pass this for you.

Open items:

- AC-8 UAT — yours whenever the live pass above is done; press J and U on an approached wet body and judge it.
